H4325.d: water; figuratively, juice; by euphemism, urine, semen

H4390.d: to fill or (intransitively) be full of, in a wide application (literally and figuratively)

H4399.d: properly, deputyship, i.e. ministry; generally, employment (never servile) or work (abstractly or concretely); also property (as the result of labor)

H4310.d: who? (occasionally, by a peculiar idiom, of things); also (indefinitely) whoever; often used in oblique construction with prefix or suffix

H4397.d: a messenger; specifically, of God, i.e. an angel (also a prophet, priest or teacher)

fb: The cave near Hebron that Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite, with its field, to bury his family. Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, Jacob and Leah all ended up there. Herod's massive stone enclosure still stands over the traditional site, now a mosque and a synagogue.

H4392.d: full (literally or figuratively) or filling (literally); also (concretely) fulness; adverbially, fully

H4376.d: to sell, literally (as merchandise, a daughter in marriage, into slavery), or figuratively (to surrender)

fb: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
Mezahab's daughter, and the mother of Mehetabel, who married Hadar, the last king of Edom in the Genesis list. Women are rare in those lists, and nothing more is said of her.
Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
Matred's father. His great claim is a granddaughter, Mehetabel, who married Hadar, the last king of Edom in the Genesis list.

H4301.d: a secret storehouse; hence, a secreted valuable (buried); generally money

fb: Manasseh's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Manasseh's son. His clan, the Machirites, were such fighters that Machir's name can stand for the whole half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan.
Man living at the time of United Monarchy
Not Manasseh's son. This Machir kept a lame son of the old royal house in his home, and later brought supplies to a king running from his own son's revolt.

H4332.d: Mishael, the name of three Israelites
fb: Daniel's compatriot living at the time of Exile and Return
One of Daniel's three friends. In Babylon he was renamed Meshach, and he lived through Nebuchadnezzar's furnace after refusing to worship the golden image.
Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Exodus and Leviticus name him twice, and he is a Levite from the wilderness years.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 3 men called Mishael. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.

H4373.d: an enumeration; by implication, a valuation

H4349.d: properly, a fixture, i.e. a basis; generally a place, especially as an abode

H4394.d: a fulfilling (only in plural), i.e. (literally) a setting (of gems), or (technically) consecration (also concretely, a dedicatory sacrifice)

H4370.d: (only in dual) drawers (from concealing the private parts)

H4385.d: a thing written, the characters, or a document (letter, copy, edict, poem)

H4340.d: a cord (of a tent); or the string (of a bow)

H4374.d: a covering, i.e. garment; specifically, a coverlet (for a bed), an awning (from the sun); also the omentum (as covering the intestines)

H4383.d: a stumbling-block, literally or figuratively (obstacle, enticement (specifically an idol), scruple)

H4347.d: a blow (in 2 Chronicles 2:10, of the flail); by implication, a wound; figuratively, carnage, also pestilence

fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness

He was one of the seventy elders chosen to share the load with Moses, and when the Spirit came on them, he and Eldad prophesied out in the camp instead of at the tent of meeting. Joshua wanted them stopped. Moses said he wished all the Lord's people were prophets.

H4317.d: Mikael, the name of an archangel and of nine Israelites
fb: Daniel names him as Israel's protector in heaven, standing against the angel princes of Persia and Greece. He is an archangel. Jude has him disputing with the devil over Moses' body, and in Revelation he leads heaven's armies against the dragon.
Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A levite from the divided-kingdom years. 1 Chronicles names him once.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him. The verse is 1 Chronicles 12:20.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years. 1 Chronicles names him once.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 10 men called Michael. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him. The verse is 1 Chronicles 5:14.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Numbers names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
One of 10 men called Michael. This one is a man from the wilderness years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 10 men called Michael. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Ezra.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Geuel's father, and Geuel was the Gadite among the twelve spies Moses sent into Canaan.

An old Moabite town given to Reuben. Joab beat the Ammonites and their Aramean allies near it in David's time, and Moab later took it back, which Isaiah mourns in his oracle against Moab. Today it is Madaba in Jordan, known for a sixth-century Byzantine floor mosaic that is the oldest surviving map of the Holy Land.

H4354.d: a Makirite or descendant of Makir

H4371.d: an assessment (as based upon a census)

H4334.d: a level, i.e. a plain (often used (with the article prefix) as a proper name of certain districts); figuratively, concord; also straightness, i.e. (figuratively) justice (sometimes adverbially, justly)

fb: A landmark on the line between Ephraim and Manasseh, near Shechem. Joshua uses it only to mark the border, and no one has found the site.

"Waters of yellowness," a river on the border of Dan, named next to Rakkon just before Joshua says Dan's land was too small and the tribe went north to take Laish. It is usually taken as the Yarkon, which still runs across the coastal plain near Tel Aviv from springs at ancient Aphek.

H4388.d: a mortar; by analogy, a socket (of a tooth)

H4321.d: Mikajah, the name of three Israelites
fb: In Judges, an Israelite who set up his own shrine with an idol and hired a wandering Levite as his private priest. Most of his verses belong to that story.
Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 3 men called Mica. This one is a Levite from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

H4318.d: Micah, the name of seven Israelites
fb: In Judges, an Israelite who set up his own shrine with an idol and hired a wandering Levite as his private priest. Most of his verses belong to that story.
Man living at the time of United Monarchy
Not the prophet. This Micah is a name in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles 8 and 9, and that is all of him.
Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
A Levite, head of a family in the divisions of 1 Chronicles 23 and 24, and nothing more is known.
Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy

The eighth-century prophet of Judah, writing at the same time as Isaiah. His short book attacks the injustice of Israel and Judah and names Bethlehem as the birthplace of a coming ruler, a line Matthew quotes in the nativity. The name means "who is like the LORD."
Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 3 men called Mica. This one is a Levite from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 3 men called Mica. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 3 men called Micah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
2 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of United Monarchy
When the lot fell on Saul to be Israel's first king, it fell first on his family within Benjamin, the Matri, and that is the only time they are named.

H4363.d: Mikmas or Mikmash, a place in Palestine
fb: Michmash, a town in Benjamin north of Jerusalem. The Philistines gathered there against Saul, and Jonathan and his armour-bearer climbed across a rocky ravine to attack their garrison, which set off a rout. Isaiah pictures the Assyrian army leaving its baggage there, and families from Michmash came back from Babylon.
Woman living at the time of United Monarchy

Saul's younger daughter. David won her by killing two hundred Philistines, and she saved his life by letting him down through a window when Saul's men came. Saul then gave her to another man; David took her back as king, but she despised him for dancing before the ark, and she had no children to the end of her life.

H4307.d: a jail (as a guard-house); also an aim (as being closely watched)

H4316.d: Mica, the name of two Israelites
fb: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a Levite from the exile and the return.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 4 men called Micha. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return, and Nehemiah is the only book that names him.
Man living at the time of United Monarchy
Mephibosheth had a young son called Micha, and that is the whole of what 2 Samuel 9:12 says.

H4323.d: properly, a container, i.e. a streamlet

fb: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

The king of Moab who paid Israel heavy tribute until Ahab died, then broke away. With the armies of Israel, Judah and Edom about to overrun him, he sacrificed his own son on the city wall to Chemosh. His own account of the revolt survives on the Moabite Stone, found at Dibon in 1868, and it names the "house of Omri."

H4320.d: Micajah, the name of two Israelites
fb: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy

The eighth-century prophet of Judah, writing at the same time as Isaiah. His short book attacks the injustice of Israel and Judah and names Bethlehem as the birthplace of a coming ruler, a line Matthew quotes in the nativity. The name means "who is like the LORD."
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 3 men called Mica. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
2 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Caleb's eldest son, and the father of Ziph, in the genealogy of Judah.

H4343.d: Macbena, a place in Palestine settled by him
fb: Woman or town of at the time of Divided Monarchy
Sheva is said to have "fathered" it in Caleb's genealogy, which probably means he founded the settlement. Where it was is unknown.

H4331.d: Mesha, a place in Arabia; also an Israelite
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A person, not a place, whatever the tag says. Shaharaim had him by his wife Hodesh, and he heads a Benjamite clan in 1 Chronicles 8:9.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Uzzi's father, a Benjamite, among the family heads who settled in Jerusalem after the exile. Nothing more is written of him.

H4382.d: a Mekerathite, or inhabitant of Mekerah
fb: It tags Hepher, one of David's mighty men in Chronicles. The place is unknown, and the two lists of these men, in 2 Samuel 23 and 1 Chronicles 11, differ on names at exactly this kind of point.

H4344.d: a Macbannite or native of Macbena
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A Gadite, good with shield and spear, who came over to David while he was hiding from Saul in the wilderness.

H4326.d: Mijamin, the name of three Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
The name of a priestly family listed under Nehemiah, and common among priests after the exile.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 3 men called Miamin. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Ezra.

H4339.d: evenness, i.e. (figuratively) prosperity or concord; also straightness, i.e. (figuratively) rectitude (only in plural with singular sense; often adverbially)

H4322.d: Mikajah, the name of an Israelite and an Israelitess
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of the officials Jehoshaphat sent round Judah to teach the law.
Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
Mother of King Abijah of Judah, probably the woman called Maacah elsewhere.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Ezra's register of men who had married foreign wives and agreed to give them up includes him.
Jewish families back from Babylon resettled this town in the Negev of Judah. Nehemiah lists it next to Ziklag, and nobody has found where it stood.

H4355.d: to tumble (in ruins); figuratively, to perish

fb: Six psalms carry it in their heading. Whether it is musical or literary, nobody is sure.

H4384.d: a stumbling-block, but only figuratively (fall, enticement [idol])

H4302.d: something planted, i.e. the place (a garden or vineyard), or the thing (a plant, figuratively or men); by implication, the act, planting

H4360.d: something perfect, i.e. a splendid garment

fb: Daniel's compatriot living at the time of Exile and Return
Mishael's Babylonian name. He was one of Daniel's three friends, and they came out of Nebuchadnezzar's furnace unhurt after refusing to bow to the golden image.
Daniel's compatriot living at the time of Exile and Return
One of Daniel's three friends. In Babylon he was renamed Meshach, and he lived through Nebuchadnezzar's furnace after refusing to worship the golden image.
Daniel's compatriot living at the time of Exile and Return
Mishael's Babylonian name. He was one of Daniel's three friends, and they came out of Nebuchadnezzar's furnace unhurt after refusing to bow to the golden image.

H4389.d: dell; the Maktesh, a place in Jerusalem
fb: "The mortar," a hollow in or near Jerusalem where merchants and silversmiths worked. Zephaniah calls out to its people when he announces judgment on the city's trade. It is generally thought to be a low market quarter, maybe in the Tyropoeon Valley.
